clue.text: Hesitate to put bet on horse past its prime

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the betting word comes after

parts.note: something past its prime is old
to put a bet on a runner is to back it

explanation.surface: A punter dithers about wagering on an elderly nag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' tells you the betting word comes after the horse pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to refrain or show reluctance, which is what hesitating amounts to.

clue.text: Interfere with the selection of food and drink

definitions.text: the selection of food and drink
definitions.meaning: a wicker basket of picnic or Christmas provisions

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to impede; the noun is a basket of provisions, as in a festive gift box of treats.

clue.text: It's attractive to see some French style

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
des is French for some
tone means style or manner

explanation.surface: A French way of doing things is appealing to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetic stone draws iron to it, so it literally attracts.

clue.text: Bale out of African organisation to achieve stability

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the word bale wraps the organisation

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: Quit an African body to bring about steadiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale out of' looks like leaving, but 'out of' puts BALE outside ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance is equilibrium, a steady even state, which is what stability means.

clue.text: Unfinished prison block

indicators.note: unfinished means the prison word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: chokey is British slang for prison

explanation.surface: A cell block in a jail that was never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke a pipe is to clog or obstruct it, the verb sense of block.

clue.text: Stretches into the future — and the past!

definitions.meaning: tightens or strains, as muscles do

definitions.text: into the future — and the past!
definitions.meaning: grammatical forms of a verb that place it in the future or the past

explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that tightens is said to do so; and verbs have forms called this for future and past time.

clue.text: Ingenious underwater discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the clever word follows the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England, so water stands for it
cute can mean clever or shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever release of something beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwater' is one printed word doing two things: 'under' places the clever word below, and 'water' is the River Exe, which flows through Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a duty is to carry it out, the same as discharging it.

clue.text: Earth in decay

definitions.meaning: soil dug out of an excavation and heaped up

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names dug-out soil from mining or digging; the verb means to rot, as food does.

clue.text: Avoid making a point that is on record

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit over the record

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Dodge the issue by raising a point already on file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts S and IDEST above EP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something by stepping aside is to dodge or avoid it.

clue.text: Undergraduates reported to be anxious over marks

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the sounded word sits on top of the marks
reported means spoken, so the fretting word is given a spelling with the same sound

parts.note: to stew is to fret or be anxious
dents are marks or impressions

explanation.surface: University students are said to worry about their grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns STEW into STU, said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates are those studying for a first degree at university.

clue.text: Moderate traffic likely here

definitions.meaning: the centre of the street, where vehicles run

explanation.definitionFit: A centrist, unextreme stance is described with this phrase, which literally names the centre of a street where cars pass.

clue.text: Cornerstone of foreign city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The founding stone of a church in some city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental core, as a cornerstone is the basis of a building or idea.

clue.text: Loud gas explosion in island capital

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A noisy gas blast in the chief town of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges LOUD and GAS. Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the chief town and seat of government of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Greek god poisoned in agony

indicators.note: being in agony means writhing about, so the letters twist into another order

explanation.surface: A deity of Greece has been poisoned and is suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Olympian deity of the sea in Greek myth.

clue.text: Diplomatic move charmed wayward sweetheart

indicators.note: wayward means straying out of line, so the letters go astray
heart picks the central letter of the word sweet

explanation.surface: An envoy's manoeuvre charmed an unruly lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is one printed word read as two: 'heart' picks the centre of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal diplomatic step or representation made to another government.

clue.text: Develop diet — without sugar ultimately

indicators.note: without signals that a letter is taken away from the dieting word

parts.note: to diet is to cut down, or reduce, one's weight

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word sugar

explanation.surface: Build up a diet while cutting out sugar in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R, the last letter of 'sugar', and 'without' removes it from REDUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or bring forth something latent, a sense close to develop.

clue.text: In one article I'm creating perfect harmony

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the article and I'm go within the word for one

parts.note: unity means oneness, the state of being one
an is the indefinite article
I'm gives IM, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Inside one newspaper article I'm making a case for total agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like a number to abbreviate, but here it is the whole word for oneness that the other pieces sit within.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimity is complete agreement of everyone, total accord.

clue.text: Broadcast protected from interference

definitions.meaning: shielded, as wiring is from electrical noise

explanation.definitionFit: A film shown on TV has been aired; a cable shielded against electrical noise has been covered with a guard.

clue.text: Many soldiers have the same belief

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
DO is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: A large group of troops all hold identical convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or principles, a set of beliefs.

clue.text: Draft published on policy

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the published word sits over the policy

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A preliminary paper has been released on government strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough sketch or first version, which is what a draft is.

clue.text: Sam hated being misrepresented in The Times — on the front page!

definitions.text: The Times — on the front page

indicators.note: misrepresenting the two words distorts them, so their letters come out reordered

explanation.surface: Sam was furious at being misquoted in a front-page story in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being misrepresented' rearranges SAM and HATED. The definition works because the title 'The Times' printed at the top of the paper's front page is exactly what this word means.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's name set in large type across the top of page one is called this.

clue.text: An architect upset to receive nothing but praise

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the turned words admit the letter for nothing
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: John Nash was a Regency architect, designer of Regent Street
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An overturned designer got nothing but compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the first two pieces to give HSANNA, and 'to receive' puts the zero inside after the H. Nash designed much of Regency London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of adoration or acclaim, used in worship as an expression of praise.

clue.text: This language may ring a bell

definitions.meaning: the clapper hanging inside a bell, which strikes it

explanation.definitionFit: A language is a speech, as in one's native speech; the clapper inside a bell shares the same name.

clue.text: He turns out to be the winner by a point

parts.note: E is east, one of the compass points
a victor is the one who wins

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly emerges as the champion by a narrow margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He turns out' reads as 'he proves to be' but is the definition: a man who turns people out of their home.
explanation.definitionFit: One who evicts tenants is literally a man who throws them out of a property.

clue.text: Athletic Tuscan keeping fit

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the words athletic Tuscan contain the answer

explanation.surface: A sporty Italian from Tuscany staying in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy, as the surface wants, but is the definition: a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine an ictus is a sudden attack or seizure, such as a stroke; a fit in that sense.

clue.text: The Moor's lieutenant is besieging north Italian town

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the lieutenant's name goes round the letter for north

parts.note: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's play; Othello is the Moor

explanation.surface: Othello's officer lays siege to a town in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassino is a town in central Italy, famous for the 1944 battle at its monastery.

clue.text: Rising, for instance, to leave the house in clerical garb

indicators.note: to leave means to depart from, so the turned letters come out of the house word

parts.note: a cottage is a small house

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the abbreviation for instance is turned round

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Getting up, perhaps, to head out of the home in a priest's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns EG into GE; 'to leave' removes it from COTTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers, a vestment.

clue.text: A night twins don't fancy, all the same

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or made up, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: The pair of siblings have no liking for one particular evening, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb meaning like, but signals rearranging A NIGHT TWINS DONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding means nevertheless or in spite of that, the sense of 'all the same'.

clue.text: Father almost took off and flew

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the father word loses its final letter

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
shed means took off, as clothes or skin

explanation.surface: Dad nearly got airborne and soared away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last D from DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed is past tense of dash, meaning rushed or hurried along, as flew can mean.

clue.text: The usual stories heard about a cripple

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the pieces go round the letter A

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard

indicators.note: heard says the word for stories is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: lies are false stories

explanation.surface: Typical tales told about one disabled person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives LYSE, sounding like the word for stories; 'about' wraps the pieces round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple something is to disable it, and to paralyse is to render it unable to move or function.
